The Earth travels around the Sun once every year. It also spins on its axis once every day, which is why we have day and night. The Earth is the third planet from the Sun, and it is the only place we know of that has life.

Water freezes at zero degrees Celsius and boils at one hundred degrees at sea level. When water freezes it expands, which is why ice floats on top of a lake and why a bottle left in the freezer can crack.

A year has twelve months and about three hundred and sixty-five days. Every fourth year is a leap year with an extra day in February. A week has seven days, and a day has twenty-four hours.

Bees visit flowers to collect nectar. While they move from flower to flower, pollen sticks to their legs and is carried to the next bloom. This helps the plants make seeds and fruit. Without bees, many of the foods we enjoy would be much harder to grow.

The human body has two hundred and six bones. The smallest bones are in the ear, and the longest is the thigh bone. Bones are strong but light, and they heal themselves after a break if they are held still.

Mountains are formed when huge pieces of the Earth's crust push against each other. The highest mountain above sea level is Mount Everest, in the Himalayas. Climbers must carry extra oxygen because the air up there is thin.

Rainbows appear when sunlight passes through raindrops. The drops bend and split the light into its colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet. You can see a rainbow when the sun is behind you and the rain is in front of you.

A triangle has three sides and three corners. A square has four equal sides. A circle has no corners at all. Shapes are all around us, in windows, wheels, books, and roofs.

Cows are mammals, which means they feed their babies milk. Other mammals include dogs, whales, bats, and people. Most mammals have fur or hair, and they are warm-blooded.

The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean on Earth. It covers more than a third of the planet's surface. The Atlantic, Indian, Southern, and Arctic oceans are smaller, but all of them are connected.

Sound travels in waves through the air. When you clap your hands, the air shakes, and the shaking moves outward until it reaches your ears. Sound cannot travel through empty space, so astronauts cannot hear each other without radios.

Lightning is a giant spark of electricity in the sky. It heats the air around it so quickly that the air expands and makes a loud boom, which we call thunder. Because light travels faster than sound, we see lightning before we hear thunder.

Trees take in carbon dioxide and give off oxygen. Their roots hold the soil in place and soak up water, and their leaves provide shade. A single large oak tree can be home to hundreds of different insects, birds, and small animals.

Penguins are birds that cannot fly, but they are excellent swimmers. Their wings have become flippers, and their feathers are packed tightly to keep out the cold water. Most penguins live in the Southern Hemisphere.

The Sun is a star. It is a huge ball of hot gas that gives us light and heat. It is so big that more than a million Earths could fit inside it, yet it is only an average-sized star compared to others in the sky.

Many people around the world speak more than one language. Mandarin Chinese has the most native speakers, followed by Spanish and English. Learning a new language can help you meet new friends and understand other cultures.

A compass has a magnetized needle that always points toward the north. The Earth acts like a very large magnet, and the needle lines up with its magnetic field. Sailors used compasses for hundreds of years to find their way across the sea.

Honey never spoils. Jars of honey found in ancient tombs thousands of years old were still safe to eat. It is very sweet, has little water in it, and is slightly acidic, so bacteria cannot grow in it.

Caterpillars turn into butterflies in four stages. First there is an egg, then a larva, which is the caterpillar. Next comes the pupa, where the caterpillar rests inside a chrysalis. Finally an adult butterfly comes out and dries its wings.

A rectangle has two long sides and two short sides. The area of a rectangle is found by multiplying its length by its width. For example, a rectangle that is five meters long and three meters wide has an area of fifteen square meters.

The library is a place where you can borrow books for free. Most libraries also have computers, quiet reading spaces, and story time for children. A librarian can help you find a book on nearly any topic you can think of.

Deserts are places that get very little rain, less than twenty-five centimeters a year. Not all deserts are hot. Antarctica is the largest desert in the world, and it is covered in ice. Plants and animals in deserts have special ways to save water.

The heart is a muscle about the size of a fist. It pumps blood through the body, carrying oxygen and food to every part. An average heart beats around one hundred thousand times each day.

Volcanoes are openings in the Earth where melted rock, called magma, comes to the surface. When magma is outside the volcano, it is called lava. Over time, layers of cooled lava can build a tall cone-shaped mountain.

Elephants are the largest land animals. They use their trunks to drink, smell, pick up food, and greet each other. A baby elephant can stand up within an hour of being born and is looked after by the whole herd.

The metric system uses meters for length, grams for weight, and liters for volume. It is easy to use because every unit is based on ten. A kilometer is a thousand meters, and a kilogram is a thousand grams.

Autumn is the season when many trees lose their leaves. Leaves are green in the summer because of chlorophyll. When the days grow shorter, the chlorophyll fades, and we see the yellow, orange, and red colors that were hiding underneath.

The first airplane flight was made by the Wright brothers in 1903. It lasted only twelve seconds and covered about thirty-six meters. Today, large airplanes carry hundreds of passengers across entire oceans in just a few hours.

Music is made of rhythm, melody, and harmony. Rhythm is the pattern of beats, melody is the tune you can sing, and harmony is when different notes are played together. Instruments can be struck, plucked, bowed, or blown.

A map is a drawing of a place seen from above. It uses symbols to show roads, rivers, buildings, and borders. Many maps have a scale that tells you how a small distance on the paper matches a larger one on the ground.

Frogs begin life in water as tiny tadpoles with tails and no legs. As they grow, they develop back legs, then front legs, and their tails shrink away. Adult frogs can live on land and in water, and they catch insects with their sticky tongues.

Sleep is important for health. During sleep the body repairs itself and the brain sorts through the things that happened during the day. Most children need between nine and eleven hours of sleep each night.

The Great Wall of China is a series of walls built over many centuries to protect the country. It is thousands of kilometers long, and it winds across mountains, deserts, and grasslands. Some parts are well preserved, and visitors can walk along them.

Computers follow instructions called programs. A program is a list of steps written in a language that the machine can understand. Even a simple program, such as one that adds two numbers, is built from many tiny steps.

Moss is a small green plant that grows in damp, shady places. It has no real roots, so it takes in water through its leaves. Moss helps to hold moisture in the soil and gives small insects a place to live.

The tides are caused mainly by the pull of the moon's gravity on the oceans. Twice a day the sea rises up the shore, and twice a day it falls back again. Fishing boats and beachcombers often plan their day around the tides.

Recycling means turning old materials into new things. Glass bottles can be melted and made into new bottles. Paper can be pulped and made into new sheets. Recycling saves energy and keeps trash out of the ground and the sea.
